Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old housekeeper with 3–4 months of painful, itchy, cracked palmar skin, likely irritant/contact dermatitis from cleaning agents and inconsistent glove use; treated with topical steroid and frequent emollients; advised strict trigger avoidance and follow-up in 10–14 days.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful, itchy, cracked skin of the hands, mainly the palms; severity now interfering with work.
- Onset/duration: Began ~3–4 months ago.
- Course: Worsened to the point of significant pain and functional limitation; required 3 days off work.
- Exacerbating factors: Occupational exposure to cleaning products; inconsistent glove use (typically gloves used for bathrooms, not always for bedrooms/corridors); job change to hotel housekeeping ~4 months ago.
- Relieving/attempted treatments: OTC emollient (E45) ineffective; OTC antihistamine ineffective (name not documented).
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent pruritus; no spontaneous bleeding, but bleeding occurs after scratching; generalized mild skin dryness (e.g., legs).
- Pertinent negatives: No fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel issues, or urinary symptoms; appetite and oral intake maintained.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus. No known prior dermatologic diagnoses (no eczema/dermatitis previously diagnosed). No history of asthma or bowel disease reported.

Medications:
- Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- OTC E45 emollient previously used (dose/frequency not documented).
- OTC antihistamine previously used (name/dose/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug or general allergies.

Social History:
- Occupation: Housekeeper at a hotel; recent job change ~4 months ago; frequent exposure to cleaning agents; inconsistent glove use.
- Work impact: Missed work for the past 3 days due to hand pain.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: A couple of pints per week.
- Other: Reports generally low water intake.

Family History:
- Diabetes present in family.
- No known family history of skin conditions, asthma, or bowel problems.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Hand dermatitis (suspected irritant/contact dermatitis due to occupational exposure)
  - Assessment: 3–4 months of painful, itchy, cracked palmar skin; temporal association with hotel housekeeping job and inconsistent glove use; systemic symptoms absent; OTC emollient and antihistamine ineffective.
  - Plan:
    - Trigger avoidance: Wear protective gloves consistently when cleaning.
    - Topical therapy: Prescribed topical steroid cream for inflammation (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Emollients: Prescribed stronger emollient; apply generously 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
    - Follow-up: Reassess in 10–14 days; return sooner if worsening, spreading, or not improving.
    - Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy.
- Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
  - Assessment: Known T2DM; no acute concerns discussed.
  - Plan: Continue current metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); no changes discussed during this visit.

- General Plan items:
  - Education provided on consistent glove use and skin care (liberal emollient application).
  - Safety-net advice: Return earlier for worsening symptoms or lack of improvement.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements: Vitals; detailed skin exam findings; specific topical steroid name and dosing schedule; exact emollient product name; complete medication list with doses/frequencies; diabetes control status (e.g., glucose logs/A1c); occupational exposure details (specific chemicals); immunization status.
- Internal conflicts: Initial complaint mentioned “fingers,” later clarified as mainly “palms”; bleeding denied initially but later confirmed only after scratching (no spontaneous bleeding). Conflict noted and clarified.
- Transcript quality: Some sections were partially inaudible/unclear; no lab or exam data provided; overall history adequate for initial assessment.
